proposal.explanation: The test failure (0 actual bytes vs 20 expected) revealed a deadlock in the upsizing adapter (OUTPUT_WIDTH > SOURCE_WIDTH) when the downstream ready signal is bursty. The root cause was twofold: (1) the combinational/sequential logic was mixed in `always_comb` blocks, causing synthesis/simulation mismatches, and (2) the state machine incorrectly drove the *input* `output_axis_tready` (an input port) instead of the *output* `input_axis_tready`. This created a signal contention that prevented the adapter from ever asserting `output_axis_tvalid`. The fix restructures all generate blocks into clean `always_comb` (combinational) and `always_ff @(posedge clk)` (sequential) sections. For the upsizing paths, a clear 3-state machine (WAIT_FIRST, WAIT_SECOND, WAIT_OUTPUT_READY) assembles a full output word from two input beats, asserts `output_axis_tvalid` only when a word is ready, and waits for `output_axis_tready` before accepting new beats. The downsizing path is similarly refactored with a beat counter and explicit handshake. The pass-through and keep-enabled paths are also cleaned up for consistency.

review.limitation: Directed simulations plus bounded two-state comparison to a historical reference; no unbounded proof or coverage of all parameters. Fixed references are excluded from model prompts.
review.scope: S_KEEP_ENABLE=0 means every source byte is valid regardless of s_axis_tkeep. Preserve frames, byte validity and ID/DEST/USER across 8-to-8/16/32-bit paths and stalls, including enabled source masks.
